title: Design System: Quiet Junction / Sam Bai Portfolio

display.purpose: One decisive public statement at radical scale.

headline.purpose: App propositions and major window headings.

title.purpose: Compact headings inside labs and technical panels.

shadows.name: aperture-rest
shadows.purpose: Holds the live Workbench aperture above the public field.

shadows.name: aperture-hover
shadows.purpose: Confirms that the live aperture can open.

shadows.name: window-rest
shadows.purpose: Separates a movable ivory window from the cobalt desktop.

shadows.name: palette
shadows.purpose: Reserves the strongest lift for the modal command surface.

shadows.name: lab-overlay
shadows.purpose: Lifts the Subsurface start and restart prompt.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Shared spatial easing for route underlines, the aperture, Workbench reveal, and windows.

motion.name: workbench-reveal
motion.purpose: Expands the Workbench from the top-right aperture.

motion.name: window-enter
motion.purpose: Reveals an opened Workbench window with scale, opacity, and clipping.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Keeps hover, focus, and active inversions immediate.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes spatial movement while preserving legible state change.

narrative.overview:
Quiet Junction is a senior, authored operating environment disguised as a sparse public front door. Carbon grain, monumental ivory type, cobalt route light, tiny operational readouts, and square rules create a private-feeling place where restraint carries more authority than a gallery of claims.

The public layer stays quiet and exacting; the Workbench reveals the machinery behind the person. Its windows, command surfaces, local tools, and two original interactive labs make software itself the personality. The tactility comes from direct manipulation, responsive state, and material contrast—not nostalgic interface cosplay.
keyCharacteristics: Monumental Archivo Black statements paired with Azeret Mono operational telemetry.
Carbon and ivory fields routed by cobalt, with signal green reserved for live, focus, and immediate action.
Square geometry, one-pixel rules, and grain establish material without nostalgic interface cosplay.
Flat public composition gives way only to structurally elevated Workbench windows and palette.
Working software reveals personality through optional, usable experiments rather than decorative demos.

rules.name: The Cobalt Is Route Rule
rules.body: Use cobalt to show where the visitor is, what is selected, or where an interaction leads; do not spread it as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Signal Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Signal green means live, focused, or actionable. Its rarity is what makes it trustworthy.

rules.name: The Monument and Telemetry Rule
rules.body: Use display type for a decisive idea and mono type for the system around it; never let both voices compete at the same scale.

rules.name: The Collapse by Mode Rule
rules.body: Desktop supports spatial composition and direct window management; small screens support one clear active task with the same content and state.

rules.name: The Structural Lift Rule
rules.body: If a surface cannot be dragged, opened, or treated as a temporary layer, it does not earn a shadow.

rules.name: The Square Instrument Rule
rules.body: Controls should read as instruments set into a system, never as soft app-store cards or pills.

rules.name: The Working Software as Personality Rule
rules.body: Use an interactive experiment when it demonstrates real judgment or capability and remains optional; not every screen needs to be gamified.

rules.name: The Native Control Rule
rules.body: Direct manipulation must keep a legible keyboard or native-input path, visible focus, and truthful local-state language.

dos: Do pair one monumental message with quiet operational metadata.
Do use cobalt for route, selection, and current state; use signal green only for live, focus, or immediate action.
Do let optional working software reveal personality when it remains useful, truthful, and self-contained.
Do use square fields, one-pixel rules, and restrained grain before adding depth.
Do preserve keyboard, native-input, reduced-motion, and local-only state conventions wherever interaction is direct.
Do pause hidden animation work in compact single-window layouts without discarding the visitor's in-progress state.
donts: Don't turn the portfolio into a project-card résumé or a wall of interchangeable case-study tiles.
Don't drift into a generic SaaS component dashboard or rounded-card shell.
Don't clone retro-Mac chrome, icons, or window decoration; the Workbench is an original typographic operating system.
Don't use shadows on static content fields or treat cobalt and signal green as decoration.
Don't start continuous lab motion before the visitor initiates it or hide the same task behind pointer-only interaction.
